title: Assassination of John F. Kennedy: In Dallas, President John F. Kennedy is shot to death, Texas Governor John B. Connally is seriously wounded, and Vice President Lyndon B. Johnson becomes the 36th president. All television coverage for the…
text: John Bowden Connally Jr. was an American politician who served as the 39th governor of Texas from 1963 to 1969 and as the 61st United States secretary of the treasury from 1971 to 1972.

title: The Golden Age Nursing Home fire kills 63 elderly people near Fitchville, Ohio.
text: The Golden Age Nursing Home fire took place soon after 4:45 am on November 23, 1963, a mile north of Fitchville, Ohio, United States, killing 63 residents. The news of the fire was overshadowed by the assassination of President John F. Kennedy, which had occurred in Dallas, Texas on the previous day.

title: Lee Harvey Oswald, assassin of John F. Kennedy, is shot dead by Jack Ruby in Dallas on live national television. Later that night, a hastily arranged program, A Tribute to John F. Kennedy from the Arts, featuring actors, opera singers, and…
text: Lee Harvey Oswald was a U.S. Marine veteran who assassinated John F. Kennedy, the 35th president of the United States, on November 22, 1963. Oswald was placed in juvenile detention at age twelve for truancy, during which he was assessed by a psychiatrist as "emotionally disturbed" because of the lack of normal family life.

title: Vietnam War: President Johnson confirms that the United States intends to continue supporting South Vietnam militarily and economically.
text: The Vietnam War was an armed conflict in Vietnam, Laos, and Cambodia fought between North Vietnam (Democratic Republic of Vietnam) and South Vietnam (Republic of Vietnam) and their allies. North Vietnam was supported by China and the Soviet Union, while South Vietnam was supported by the United States and other anti-communist nations.

title: President Kennedy is buried at Arlington National Cemetery. Schools around the nation do not have class on that day, and millions around the world watch the funeral on live television.
text: Arlington National Cemetery is the largest cemetery in the United States National Cemetery System, one of two maintained by the United States Army. More than 400,000 people are buried in its 639 acres in Arlington County, Virginia.

title: President Johnson establishes the Warren Commission to investigate the assassination of President Kennedy.
text: The President's Commission on the Assassination of President Kennedy, known unofficially as the Warren Commission, was established by President Lyndon B. Johnson through Executive Order 11130 on November 29, 1963, to investigate the assassination of United States president John F. Kennedy that had taken place on November 22, 1963. The U.S. Congress passed Senate Joint Resolution 137 authorizing the presidentially-…

title: Wendell Scott becomes the first African-American driver to win a NASCAR race at Speedway Park.
text: Wendell Oliver Scott Sr. was an American stock car racing driver.

title: Frank Sinatra Jr. is kidnapped at Harrah's Lake Tahoe.
text: Francis Wayne Sinatra, known professionally as Frank Sinatra Jr., was an American jazz and big band singer, songwriter, conductor and actor. He was the second child and only son of singer and actor Frank Sinatra and his first wife, Nancy Barbato Sinatra, the younger brother of singer and actress Nancy Sinatra, and the older brother of television producer Tina Sinatra.

title: A lightning strike causes the crash of Pan Am Flight 214 near Elkton, Maryland, killing 81 people.
text: Pan Am Flight 214 was a scheduled flight of Pan American World Airways from San Juan, Puerto Rico, to Baltimore, and then to Philadelphia in the United States. On December 8, 1963, while flying from Baltimore to Philadelphia, the Boeing 707 crashed near Elkton, Maryland.

title: The X-20 Dyna-Soar spaceplane program is cancelled.
text: The Boeing X-20 Dyna-Soar was a United States Air Force (USAF) program to develop a spaceplane that could be used for a variety of military missions, including aerial reconnaissance, bombing, space rescue, satellite maintenance, and as a space interceptor to sabotage enemy satellites. The program ran from 24 October 1957, to 10 December 1963, cost US$660 million ($6.94 billion in 2024 dollars), and was cancelled j…

title: Chuck Yeager becomes the first pilot to make an emergency ejection in the full pressure suit needed for high altitude flights.
text: Charles Elwood Yeager was a United States Air Force officer, flying ace, and record-setting test pilot who in October 1947 became the first pilot in history confirmed to have exceeded the speed of sound in level flight. Yeager was raised in Hamlin, West Virginia.

title: Baldwin Hills Dam disaster floods South Los Angeles, causing five deaths.
text: The Baldwin Hills Dam disaster occurred on December 14, 1963 in the Baldwin Hills neighborhood of South Los Angeles, when the dam containing the Baldwin Hills Reservoir suffered a catastrophic failure and flooded the residential neighborhoods surrounding it. It began with signs of lining failure, followed by increasingly serious leakage through the dam at its east abutment.

title: Walt Disney releases his 18th feature-length animated motion picture, The Sword in the Stone, about the boyhood of King Arthur. It is Disney's final animated film to be released during his lifetime, before his death in 1966.
text: Walter Elias Disney was an American animator, film producer, voice actor, and entrepreneur. A pioneer of the American animation industry, he introduced several developments in the production of cartoons.

title: The Beatles' songs "I Want to Hold Your Hand" and "I Saw Her Standing There" are released in the U.S., marking the beginning of full-scale Beatlemania.
text: The Beatles were an English rock band formed in Liverpool in 1960. The band comprised John Lennon, Paul McCartney, George Harrison and Ringo Starr.

title: David. H. Frisch and James H. Smith prove that the radioactive decay of mesons is slowed by their motion (see Einstein's special relativity and general relativity).
text: David Henry Frisch was an American physicist who helped develop the atom bomb in World War II and later became active in the disarmament movement. He was also the husband of Rose Epstein Frisch.

title: Civil rights movement (1954–68)
text: The civil rights movement was a social movement in the United States from 1954 to 1968 which aimed to abolish legalized racial segregation, discrimination, and disenfranchisement in the country, which most commonly affected African Americans. The movement had origins in the Reconstruction era in the late 19th century, and modern roots in the 1940s and in Mahatma Gandhi's nonviolent movement in India.

title: “Pipeline” by The Chantays
text: "Pipeline" is a surf rock instrumental by the Chantays, which was recorded in July 1962.

title: “Surf City” by Jan and Dean
text: "Surf City" is a 1963 song recorded by the American music duo Jan and Dean about a fictitious surf spot where there are "two girls for every boy". Written by Brian Wilson and Jan Berry, it was the first surf song to become a national number-one hit.

title: “It's My Party” by Lesley Gore
text: "It's My Party" is the debut song recorded by American singer Lesley Gore on her debut studio album I'll Cry If I Want To. It was released as her debut single on April 5, 1963, by Mercury Records.

title: “Blame It on the Bossa Nova” by Eydie Gormé
text: "Blame It on the Bossa Nova" is a song written by Cynthia Weil and Barry Mann that became a 1963 hit single for Eydie Gormé, reaching No. 7 on the Hot 100 in Billboard in March 1963.
wiki: Blame It on the Bossa Nova

title: “You Can't Sit Down” by The Dovells
text: "You Can't Sit Down" is a song originally recorded as an instrumental in 1959 as "Can't Sit Down" by the Bim Bam Boos, and popularized by the 1963 version by the Dovells, which included lyrics and vocals. The Dovells version of the song peaked at No.3 on the Billboard Hot 100 chart and has been covered by many artists, including the Shangri-Las and Bruce Springsteen.
listen: You Can't Sit Down The Dovells

title: “Heat Wave” by Martha and the Vandellas
text: "Heat Wave" Heat Wave") is a 1963 song written by Holland–Dozier–Holland. It was first made popular by the Motown vocal group Martha and the Vandellas, who issued it as a single on July 10, 1963, on the Motown subsidiary Gordy Records.
listen: Heat Wave Martha and the Vandellas

title: “Painted, Tainted Rose” by Al Martino
text: Jasper Cini, known professionally as Al Martino, was an American Jazz and traditional pop and standards singer. He had his greatest success as a singer between the early 1950s and mid-1970s, being described as "one of the great Italian American pop crooners", and became known as an actor, particularly for his role as singer Johnny Fontane in The Godfather.

title: Leonardo da Vinci's Mona Lisa is exhibited in the United States for the first (and only) time, for a period of four weeks, at the National Gallery of Art in Washington, D.C. During this time it was viewed by over half a million people.
text: Leonardo di ser Piero da Vinci, better known as Leonardo da Vinci, was an Italian polymath of the High Renaissance who was active as a painter, draughtsman, engineer, scientist, anatomist, sculptor, and architect. While his fame initially rested on his achievements as a painter, he has also become known for his notebooks, in which he made drawings and notes on a variety of subjects, including anatomy, astronomy, b…

title: The David Mirvish Gallery is opened in Toronto by David Mirvish.
text: David Mirvish, is a Canadian theatre producer, impresario, and art collector. He owns and operates Toronto-based theatrical production company Mirvish Productions, which he founded with his father in 1986.

title: Museum of Contemporary Art (Skopje) opens in Yugoslavia.
text: The Contemporary Art Museum is a contemporary art museum located in Skopje, North Macedonia. It is the biggest and most modern museum in the country.
